prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There isn’t one universal “best” roofing company for hurricane‑rated replacements in Miami — the best contractor for you depends on your ZIP code, roof type (asphalt shingle, tile, metal), whether it’s an insurance job, your timeline and budget. I can help find and vet local contractors if you tell me your ZIP code and roof type. Below are practical steps, what to look for, red flags, and next actions so you can pick the best contractor for your situation.

How to choose the best hurricane‑rated roofer
- Verify licensing and insurance
  - Florida roofing/contractor license (search DBPR/Contractor license lookup).
  - Current general liability and workers’ comp insurance — ask for COI listing you as “certificate holder.”
- Confirm Miami‑Dade / Florida Building Code compliance
  - Contractor should install products that have Miami‑Dade Notice of Acceptance (NOA) or Florida Product Approval when required.
  - Installation must meet the current Florida Building Code wind‑uplift and fastening requirements.
- Manufacturer and workmanship warranties
  - Request manufacturer’s warranty for the shingles/metal and a contractor workmanship warranty (get both in writing).
- Experience and reputation
  - At least several years doing hurricane‑rated roof installs in Miami; ask for recent local references and photos.
  - Check BBB, Google/Yelp reviews, and local community groups.
- Written estimate and scope
  - Get at least 3 written bids with clear scope: materials (brand/model), underlayment, flashing, fastener type/nail pattern, removal of old roofing, disposal, permit handling, cleanup, and timeline.
- Permits and inspections
  - Contractor should obtain required permits and schedule final inspections.
- Price and payment terms
  - Avoid paying large upfront cash sums. Typical deposits are moderate; final payment after inspections and lien waivers. Beware of “storm chasers” soliciting immediately after storms.

Key technical items to require for hurricane‑rated roof
- Miami‑Dade NOA–approved products (for areas requiring it).
- High‑wind rated shingles or Class 4 impact‑resistant options if you need impact protection.
- Proper underlayment / secondary water barrier.
- Correct nailing pattern, ring‑shank or stainless fasteners as appropriate.
- Roof deck attachment: straps, clips, or other tie‑down methods required by FBC.
- Flashing and penetration details per code.

Red flags / scams
- Contractor solicits door‑to‑door the week after a storm offering “special” pricing.
- Pressure to sign immediately or to use cash only.
- No physical office or no local references.
- No permit pulled or suggests “we don’t need a permit.”
- Extremely low bid far below others.

Typical cost ranges (very approximate)
- Asphalt shingle replacement (hurricane-rated materials and proper installation): roughly $350–$650 per roofing square (100 sq ft) depending on roof complexity, materials, and whether old roofing is removed.
- Tile or metal roofs cost more — often significantly higher per square.
Get exact quotes — local conditions and roof complexity change prices a lot.

Next steps I can do for you
- If you give your ZIP code and roof type (shingles/tile/metal) I can:
  - Find 3–5 well‑reviewed Miami contractors for hurricane‑rated replacements.
  - Prepare an email/text checklist you can send to contractors to get consistent bids.
  - Look up a contractor’s license and Miami‑Dade NOA/product info if you have names.

Which would you like to do next?
